failure.symptom: Port N is listening was printed, then the follow-up's python3 socket.create_connection raised ConnectionRefusedError, so serve_worker returned step_failed (sh failed, exit status 1) and the test's unwrap panicked at native/javascript.rs:439

root_cause.classification: test fixture race; not a production readiness defect and not an environment fault
root_cause.explanation: The fixture's Python server exited on the first connection it accepted after the marker file existed, without checking that the connection came from the follow-up command. serve_worker proves readiness with a TCP connect probe (listening()) that it closes immediately; the kernel completes that handshake from the listen backlog, so the probe succeeds whether or not the server process has called accept yet. If the server accepted the probe, or got as far as checking the marker, only after the follow-up's sh had touched the marker, it treated the probe as the follow-up, closed its listening socket and exited. The follow-up's own python3 needs tens of milliseconds to start, so it then connected to a closed port and was refused. A second path with the same cause: a stray connection on a recycled free port (metro_reload_posts_to_the_reload_endpoint deliberately connects to freed ports; a_busy_port_or_a_failing_server_is_reported probes its own) ended the server the same way. The comment added in 92d72ab ('It checks only after an accept, so it cannot exit before the follow-up's own connection arrives') assumed the probe was always handled before the marker appeared, and that assumption is false under load.
root_cause.production_check: serve_worker (native/javascript.rs) runs the follow-up commands only after listening() connected successfully, i.e. after the server's port accepted a TCP connection. That is the correct readiness contract and is unchanged. A real Metro server simply serves and closes the probe connection.

baseline_intermittent.note: Not reproduced by plain repetition on this machine; the failure needs one particular scheduling order, which the qualification run (CTest with Qt suites around it) hit once.

forced_reproduction.method: Temporary in-tree experiment module (removed before the commit; source kept in .scratch/qfix/race_experiment.rs) calling the real serve_worker with (a) a 0.1 s pause after accept, modelling a server descheduled after the kernel completed the probe handshake, and (b) a stray connection after the marker, modelling a parallel test on a recycled port. In both cases the follow-up waits 0.3 s before connecting.
forced_reproduction.old_fixture: late probe: step_failed with ConnectionRefusedError; stray connection: step_failed with ConnectionRefusedError (the exact qualification symptom)
forced_reproduction.new_fixture: late probe: ok; stray connection: ok
forced_reproduction.repetitions: 1 run plus 10 repetitions with --test-threads 4: all 4 expectations held 11/11

evidence.readiness_assertion_preserved: Mutation check: with serve_worker's wait loop disabled (while false && !listening(port)), the fixed test fails with step_failed and ConnectionRefusedError in 0.03 s. Source restored before the commit, and the committed file is byte-identical to the tested one.

change.diff: 1 file, 10 insertions, 5 deletions, test module only
details: The follow-up command now connects and sends the payload 'then'. The server reads each accepted connection up to EOF (16 bytes at most) and exits only on exactly that payload. The readiness probe (EOF at once) and stray connections (other or no payload, or a read error) are served, and the server keeps listening.

Bounded: the listening socket has a 20 s accept timeout and each accepted connection a 5 s read timeout. If no follow-up ever arrives, the server exits with an error and serve_worker reports server_failed, so the test fails instead of hanging. This adds no delay on the passing path, and no sleep or timeout was raised to hide the race.
The marker file and assert!(marker.exists()) are kept. The 0.3 s pre-bind delay, which exercises serve_worker's wait-for-port loop, is unchanged.
serve_worker, the operation registry, the CLI/MCP contracts, QML, translations and fonts are unchanged.
